evidence: Swap test fails: a seed library, toy library or village-hall equipment hire could use every identity-carrying element unchanged (wordmark set in bold body text beside a small stroke wrench, sage-grey ground, one dark-green accent on buttons and availability chips, one geometric sans, bordered white cards). Only the copy (tool names, deposits, Wed/Sat sessions, 14 Mill Lane) is bound to Fernhill.

Category-guess test fails: the predicted default for a small community/public booking service is a government-service-style form: off-white ground, one green action colour, bold sans headings, red error summary box, underlined links, label/value summary tables. find/default/1280-light, confirm/errors/375-light and done/default/1280-light match it element for element.

Similar-prompt test fails: a brief for 'a parish council booking page for the hall and its folding tables' would very likely land on the same white cards with a repeated generic icon tile, green Search/Continue buttons and a summary-list confirm page.

The only element derived from the product's mechanism is the pick-up calendar marking session days as 'Open' (green dot at 375); it is a standard date grid and is partly hidden by the sticky Reserve bar (tool/default/1280-light), so it cannot carry the identity.
Tool thumbnails are the same wrench glyph in a pale-green square on all 10 items (find/default/1280-light), so the one place the real tools could appear shows nothing of them.
